main_text.head: PETRI CASSIODORI AD ANGLOS EPISTOLA, SUPER EXTREMA ANGLIÆ EXPILATIONE AC SERVITUTE PER PAPAS CIRCA ANNUM DOMINI 1302, UT ROM. TYRANNIDIS IUGUM EXCUTERENT.
main_text.p: Exemplo codice ad sanctum Albani descripta.

Ecclesiæ nobili Anglicanæ, in luto et latere ancillatæ, Petrus filius Cassiodori, miles catholicus, pugil Iesu Christi devotus, salutem, et captiuitatis iugum abiicere, et brauium accipere libertatis. Super cathedram Moysi sederunt Scribæ et Pharisæi, etc.
Sequitur: Cui comparabo te, vel cui assimilabo te Hierusalem filia? cui exæquabo te, uirgo filia Syon? magna enim est tua contritio, velut mare fracta; est sine solatio, tota die mærore fracta.

Data es in manus eius, de quo non potes surgere absque auxilio subleuantis. Nam scribæ et pharisæi super cathedram Moysi sedentes, principes Romani hostes tibi in capite fixi, sua phylacteria dilatantes, ambientes locupletari tuorum offium ex medullis, grauia et importabilia in tuis et tuorum ministrorum imponunt humeris onera: et ultra quam decet, te constituunt sub tributo, quæ liberæ fueras ab antiquo. page.notes: Scan is a 16th/17th century Latin printing with a worn, faded page. Several words are doubtful and were reconstructed from context rather than read letter by letter; they are not marked here and should be checked against the scan: "Exemplo"/"Exemplo" (first line after heading), "fracta", "subleuantis", "offium", "ministrorum", "pontificem" line-end and the final word "ficem" which appears to be the start of "pontificem" continued from the previous line. Page is likely best treated as a low-confidence transcription. Heading lines at top are printed in the running-head and heading style; the heading is set as a level 1 division title.
